observations: Photo 0: Silver HP laptop in tablet mode, screen off, showing HP logo on screen bezel, 'ELITEBOOK' text below keyboard, Intel Core sticker on palm rest, keyboard appears to be backlit.
Photo 1: Back of the laptop showing HP logo, barcode sticker with number '110569159', ventilation grille, and regulatory labels. No visible model number.
Photo 2: Front view of the screen in tablet mode, showing a glossy black screen with reflections, no visible damage or dead pixels from this angle.
All photos show a watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI JORACH LIMITED'.
The laptop is being held in a white cabinet with stacks of other laptops wrapped in plastic in the background.

claims.evidence: Model name is not visible in any photo; only 'ELITEBOOK' is readable on the keyboard bezel in photo 0. Seller's text claims the model, but no photo confirms it.
Photo 2 shows the screen being held in tablet mode, indicating a 360-degree hinge and touch capability. The screen is also glossy, typical of touch screens.
No photo shows internal components or BIOS/OS screen to verify RAM and SSD. Cannot be confirmed remotely.
Intel sticker visible in photo 0, but no model number or generation is readable. Cannot confirm CPU remotely.
Photo 0 shows a backlit keyboard with illuminated keys, indicating keyboard light is present.

risks.risk: The laptop may not be the claimed model (HP EliteBook x360 1030 G2)
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model label on the bottom or inside the lid, or a BIOS screen showing the model name.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic HP EliteBook 2-in-1, which is lower than the 1030 G2.

risks.risk: The CPU may not be a 7th gen Core i7
risks.proof: A screenshot of the system information or BIOS showing the CPU model.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a lower-end CPU model, reducing value.

risks.risk: RAM or SSD may not match the claimed 8GB and 256GB
risks.proof: A screenshot of the system information or disk management showing installed RAM and SSD capacity.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if it has less RAM or smaller SSD, reducing value.

risks.risk: Screen may have dead pixels or damage not visible in photos
risks.proof: A video or photo of the screen displaying a solid white or black screen to check for dead pixels or cracks.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if screen is faulty, reducing value.

risks.risk: Battery may be degraded or not working
risks.proof: A video showing the laptop running on battery with battery percentage and health displayed.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if battery is dead or degraded, reducing value.

proof_requests: A clear photo of the model label on the bottom or inside the lid.
A screenshot of the system information showing CPU, RAM, and SSD details.
A video or photo of the screen displaying solid white and black to check for dead pixels.
A video showing the laptop running on battery with battery health displayed.
response.reason: The model identity cannot be confirmed from the photos alone, and key specifications like CPU, RAM, and SSD are unverifiable remotely. The screen and keyboard light are supported, but without proof of the claimed model and specs, the item cannot be priced accurately. The risks of misrepresentation are high, so proof is required before pricing.
